_doc: THE RECORDED MAP from exit-relevant harness FLAG to M20 coverage-matrix LEVER COLUMN. It exists to satisfy BL-20260810-EXIT-LEVER-SPACE-UNDER-ENUMERATED's first criterion -- 'every exit-relevant harness flag maps to a matrix column OR a recorded n/a with a reason' -- and it is checked, not merely written: scripts/ops/exit_lever_map.py re-enumerates the harnesses and FAILS on any candidate flag this file does not cover, so it cannot silently go stale as flags are added. ⚠️ THREE STATES, NEVER COLLAPSED. `mapped_to_column` is a lever the matrix already grades. `recorded_na` is a flag that is NOT an exit lever, with the reason stated -- the criterion's own escape hatch. `needs_column` is the finding: an exit lever the matrix CANNOT express, which is neither of the other two and must not be filed as either. Collapsing needs_column into recorded_na would make the gap disappear by wording.

population.how_the_harness_set_was_chosen: NOT by hand. It is the set the matrix's own 52 rows route to, resolved by scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::classify over each row's `strategy`: donchian 23, pullback 19, scalp 8, squeeze 1, fvg 1. ⚠️ THIS IS WHY THE COUNT MOVED. The 2026-09-02 analysis on the backlog row enumerated backtest_trend.py and backtest_pullback.py only -- 42 of the 52 legs -- and so could not see any gap arising from the scalp (8), squeeze (1) or fvg (1) legs. Its answer of 3 gaps is correct FOR ITS POPULATION and understates the matrix's own.
population.candidate_rule: A flag is a CANDIDATE when its name contains any of the stated exit vocabulary (see scripts/ops/exit_lever_map.py::EXIT_VOCAB). ⚠️ This is a token rule and it is the WEAK link: it is used only to decide what must be looked at, never what the answer is. Every verdict below is a curated decision with its evidence. A flag the rule misses is invisible to the checker -- so the checker also reports the non-candidate remainder as a COUNT, which is `we did not look`, never a clean bill.

--atr-stop-mult.note: the matrix's own legend_bracket_geometry defines the column as the ENTRY BRACKET TRIPLE (tp_at_r x atr_stop_mult ...), so this flag IS one of its three terms.

--tp-r.note: the declared tp_r sentinel; per its help it is consulted only when --tp-cap-pct > 0, and the cap normally binds.

--tp-cap-pct.note: LIVE-PARITY take-profit on a CLAMPING family -- min(entry*(1+pct), entry + tp_r*risk). Production uses 0.099. ⚠️ ITS MEANING IS FAMILY-DEPENDENT AND THE TWO ARE OPPOSITE (corrected 2026-09-18, MI-312). On trend/pullback/squeeze the harness has no other source of a target, so no flag means NO take-profit and the flag is live parity. On backtest_ict_scalp.py and backtest_fvg_range.py the target comes from the strategy, whose live unit applies NO clamp -- scalp and fvg are absent from tp_venue_cap.CLAMPING_FAMILIES -- so there the DEFAULT is live parity and this flag is a COUNTERFACTUAL that departs from it. Measured on BTCUSDT 5m (n=45): a 0.099 cap was inert on 45 of 45 scalp trades, because a 1.5R target sits at ~0.95% of entry against a 9.9% clamp.

--exit-style.note: fvg_range's expression of WHERE the target sits (mid | far | tp1r). Mapped here on the matrix's OWN evidence, not on inference: its vol_trail caveat for this leg reads 'scripts/backtest_fvg_range.py has NO --trail-mult at all -- this leg exits on exit_style/tp_r, not a trailing stop'.

--atr-stop-buffer.note: fvg_range's stop leg -- 'Stop placed buffer x ATR beyond the gap / range boundary', i.e. this family's atr_stop_mult.

--atr-period.reason: An INDICATOR period feeding the ATR that the bracket and trail levers consume -- a measurement input, not an exit rule. ARGUABLE AND RECORDED AS SUCH: changing it does move every ATR-derived exit distance, so someone could reasonably call it a lever. It is n/a here because the matrix's bracket_geometry column is defined as the TRIPLE (tp_at_r x atr_stop_mult x ...) and a period change re-scales the unit those terms are expressed in rather than choosing a different rule. If a sweep ever varies it, this entry is the thing to revisit.

--exit-grain.reason: A measurement-FIDELITY knob, not a lever: it chooses the bar grain the exit levers are evaluated on (leg-bar vs sub-bar close) to isolate a harness artefact. It changes what the HARNESS can see, never what production does.

--timeout-bars.reason: NO LIVE CONSUMER -- and this is the matrix's own recorded position, not a new judgement. 33 of its 52 rows carry a caveat of the form 'a NEGATIVE measured on a harness that force-closed at `timeout_bars` while live has no time stop'. So it is a harness CONFOUND that the matrix already corrects for, and giving it a lever column would invite sweeping a rule production cannot express -- the matrix's own `blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit` state. ⚠️ This is NOT a claim that a time stop is unwanted: building the LIVE side is BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES, and if that ships, this entry flips to needs_column.

--rr-floor.reason: GRADED AND SWEPT, AND INVISIBLE. It is the proximity-to-target lever BL-20260810-EXIT-LEVER-SPACE-UNDER-ENUMERATED was filed believing did not exist; its help text is the operator's near-TP-reversal case verbatim. Swept on the fleet's own machinery (docs/research/e35-rr-floor-walkforward-2026-08-20.md, 19 legs x 3 cells = 57 leg-cell rows), and `scripts/ci/check_lever_wiring.py` confirms its cells. With no column, those 57 measured rows are invisible to anyone reading the matrix. ⚠️ A column would have to say BACKTEST-ONLY (BL-20260818-RR-FLOOR-IS-BACKTEST-ONLY-AND-CANNOT-BE-DECLARED).

--be-floor-r.reason: MI-165 break-even FLOOR, present on donchian + pullback + squeeze: once the trade has SEEN this many R, the trailing stop may never again sit below entry. It is max()-ed against the chandelier candidate, so it is a one-directional RATCHET distinct from trail_geometry rather than a setting of it. The string `be_floor` appears ZERO times anywhere in the matrix.

--be-floor-lock-r.reason: Profit-lock STEP for --be-floor-r, pullback harness only (ADA-LIVE-EXIT-REVIEW-1024, 2026-10-24): the armed floor sits at entry + k R instead of entry; 0.0 = the plain break-even floor, byte-identical. It is a SUB-KNOB of --be-floor-r, so whoever adds the be_floor column should carry it as that column's lock level rather than a column of its own. First consumer: research/queue/RQ-20261024-4ef5-01.yaml.

--sim-breakeven.reason: ict_scalp only, and it SIMULATES A LIVE MECHANISM -- 'the LIVE monitor's break-even trail (monitor_breakeven_sl: once a bar closes >= 1R in favour, SL moves to entry +/- be_offset_bps from YAML)'. So unlike --timeout-bars it has a live consumer, which is what makes its absence a gap rather than an n/a. The string `sim_breakeven` appears ZERO times in the matrix, while 8 of the matrix's 52 legs are scalp legs.

--be-arm-on-touch.reason: ict_scalp only. Its own help says it is 'only meaningful with --sim-breakeven', so it is arguably a SUB-KNOB of that lever rather than a column of its own -- recorded here as needs_column so the decision is made explicitly rather than by omission. Whoever adds the breakeven column should decide whether the arming rule is a second cell or a parameter of the first.

--no-tp.reason: A measurement-FIDELITY knob, not a lever -- the same class as --exit-grain. It DISABLES the strategy's own take-profit so the harness can observe an excursion the live target would have truncated, which is what makes a target-setting MFE distribution possible at all (MI-312). It changes what the HARNESS can see, never what production does: production always has its target, so there is no production state this flag corresponds to and a matrix column would assert one. Declared by backtest_ict_scalp.py and backtest_fvg_range.py only, because those two get their target from the strategy itself; the trend/pullback/squeeze harnesses need no such flag since --tp-cap-pct 0 already leaves them with no target.

--tp-revision.reason: TP doctrine B1 (2026-10-07): re-estimates the TP after every closed bar with the declared rule (only donchian_measured_move, src/runtime/tp_revision.py, the SAME core the live trend_donchian monitor() and the prop trail call). A target-MOVING lever, distinct from --tp-r / --tp-cap-pct (which fix the entry target). No matrix column exists for a revised target; graded by RQ-20261007-080 (scripts/research/tp_revision_sweep.py). Adding the column is a coverage-matrix schema change, a manager decision.

--tp-revision-width-mult.reason: Parameter of --tp-revision: the measured-move multiple of the Donchian channel height (swept {0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0} by RQ-20261007-080). Maps to the same future column as --tp-revision.

summary_2026_09_12.note: The four needs_column entries are the finding and are NOT fixed here: adding a column is a schema change to a 765 KB artifact that `matrix-corpus-agreement` and `matrix-config-agreement` both read, and it is one decision for the manager rather than four edits by a drain session. What this file removes is the ambiguity about WHICH four and WHY.
